title: Buying acts and recording Irma Thomas and Chris Kenner
summary: After Slim he bought acts from agencies, adding band and commission; he recorded only Slim, Irma Thomas and Chris Kenner.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Record labels, producers and the business of making albums

blocks.x: Oh, okay. So after Slim, what was your next act?

Well, after Slim, well after Slim, we started buying acts, you know. Yeah. Buying acts for five nights. And of course, you can look on the wall and see some of these. Yeah. Oh yeah. We started buying acts. And then later down the line, I told you, I record this girl, I'm a termist.
And she was in there. Right. Why'd you get involved in the film?

Well, she came to me and asked me to, she had made a record, and it wasn't so good a good record. And so she came to me and asked me to book it. And so I told her, the only thing you could do was to be, to get a record. So we got a record on her. Which one? Killing her, Imperial Labor. And it really went over for her. So she was on there ever since. Now I had, after, after Ehrman, I had another artist, Chris Kenner. I recorded him. He had several good numbers. Chris, Chris died back in L.A. So I guess you'd call him. Yeah. I remember. So that's, that's the only two, the only three artists that I recorded during my lifetime. The rest of them I just bought them, you know. I bought artists. Well, how would you work that? Well, I would call up, we'd call up, let's say, let's say we call up Shaw agents, you know. Right. And let's say Shaw has got Roscoe Robinson, or Roscoe Gardner, Ray Charles. Let's use him as a picture, you know. Okay. So we find out what you want a night. What do you get a night? Well, he gets so much a night. Well, okay, we want five nights. We want ten nights, you know. Then we get a ten night price. So we take the artists, bring them back, put them with the band, if they didn't have a band, the local band would add here. Then we in turn sell them to the club, or play them with the club, out, out, out, you know. Right. So they make, put a profit on them. The band worked, put a good profit on them. Right. So you'd up the price to the, to the club? We'd add the, we'd add the artist price, and then we'd add the band price. And if the guy wanted to buy it, we'd add maybe a $200 commission for us tonight, see. And then if the guy played it with us, we knew the time we'd play, play it just what it cost us, you see. Cause we'd buy the money up anyway, you see. Uh huh. So that's right. So I started to, during that time, quite some time. And of course I played quite many artists in my lifetime. Made some dollars and lost some dollars.
Just like a horse race, you know. You don't want to get rich.
